title: A steady-tone search finds no excess from 40 to 500 Hz at 2 to 18 seconds after GW150914
abstract: We test public H1 and L1 strain for a steady 16-second tone from 2 to 18 seconds after GW150914. The search covers 40 to 500 Hz. Minimum normalized detector power gives full-search ranks of 0.619 and 0.889 with early and late noise estimates. No tone passes the chosen empirical threshold. Separate calibration and held-out controls test false alarms and injected-signal recovery. Drifting signals and unequal detector amplitudes are also tested. The Livingston record has a continuous-wave hardware-injection flag. Small tail samples, noise drift, lines, fixed duration and the lack of a phase test limit the result. We find no new source and set no astrophysical upper limit. Code, source hashes, aggregate spectra, recovery results, a figure and retrieval steps are included. Raw strain stays external.

display.caption: The target spectrum, noise controls and held-out recovery of steady injected tones. The red dashed lines show the empirical calibration threshold.
Noise normalization changes the control tail. Frequency drift and detector amplitude ratio change recovery at fixed injected amplitude. Error bars show exact binomial 95 percent intervals.

citations.reason: Prior short-pulse test identifies the shared raw files and hardware-injection caution. No code or numerical output is reused.
